content_full:
You can now connect Picsart directly to Google Gemini to get more done. For example, you can turn a single image into a cinematic short, design a logo, or upscale a visual for a larger format, now with this new connection in Gemini. Picsart is a connected app that brings 190+ AI models and creative tools into your chat without switching between apps.

You stay in the driver’s seat. You describe what you want in your own words, and Picsart finds the right model for you, so you get more done without learning a new tool first.

How to turn on Picsart in Google Gemini

Turn on the connected app once. After that, Picsart is ready for supported creative requests in your Gemini conversations.

Three moves to get connected:

  1. Open Settings and select Personal Intelligence. Both sit in your Google Gemini settings menu.
  2. Open Connected Apps. Scroll to the section listing third-party services.
  3. Select Picsart. Switch it on and start making creative requests in the chat.

If Picsart is not in the list, check that you are signed in with the Google account that has access to connected apps. Availability and menu labels can both change during rollout.

Start with one image and take it anywhere

A single image is the starting point, not the deliverable. From there the same conversation can turn it into something else entirely, and you never open a separate editor to do it.

What one image can become:

  • A cinematic short, so a still you already like becomes motion without a separate video brief
  • A polished product shot, the version that holds up on a listing or an ad rather than in a moodboard
  • A set of variations, so a test runs on several finished options instead of one asset and an assumption

Refinement works the same way. Describe the change and it happens: the mood, the setting, or the text in the frame. You are describing an outcome rather than operating a tool.

Work that does not start from an image

Not everything begins with a file you already have. You can design a logo in the same conversation, starting from a description rather than something you upload.

Delivery is handled there too. Resize visuals for different channels when one concept has to run in several placements, or upscale for a larger format when the piece is going somewhere that punishes a small file.

Your Drive and credits are in the chat

The connection is not only generation. You can check your Picsart credits, reach your Picsart Drive, and create folders directly in the conversation.

That matters more than it sounds. Work that comes back has somewhere to go, so the output lands organized instead of accumulating in a thread you have to scroll back through later.

What sits behind the connection

The connected app is built on Picsart MCP, the same server that connects Picsart to other assistants. That is why one connection reaches a whole model catalog rather than a single fixed tool.

That range is why these requests can be so different from each other. A set of variations, a mood change, a short film, and an upscale are not the same job, and Picsart finds what fits each one.

That saves you the part that usually eats the time. There is no step where you weigh one tool against another, or learn which one handles the thing you are making.

Who can use it right now

The connected app is currently available to eligible users in the United States, in English. It is not available in other countries yet, and more regions are coming.

Turn it on and give it something to make

Open Gemini, turn on Picsart under Connected Apps, and begin with a creative request. The setup is three steps and you only do it once.
